title: Three-act rescue scriptbook for sellers & ops (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, repeatable 3-act play sellers can run with Ops/SRE when pilots hit friction (latency spikes, cost surprises, unexpected rate limits). Focus is on (1) keeping the customer confident, (2) controlling blast radius, and (3) capturing data to decide a fast next step (tune, fall back, or expand).

Intended audience:
- Sales engineers (primary)
- Field sellers and account execs (secondary)
- Platform/ops on-call and SREs (partners during pilot)

High-level approach (three acts):
Act 1 — The Hook (first 3–5 minutes)
- Goal: reassure + surface the right SLA/cost tradeoffs.
- Slide 1: "What we saw / why you noticed it" (simple signal snapshot: p95 latency, error spike, tokens per request)
- Speaker notes: "We saw an increase in p95 from 180ms to 1.2s during that window — that usually maps to (a) hot KV cache misses, (b) burst hitting non-dedicated capacity, or (c) long context lengths. We’ll triage live, and we have safe fallbacks ready"
- Quick scripts: "Thanks for flagging this — we think it's actionable in the next 15–30 minutes. We’re going to run a short diagnostic and then propose a temporary fallback so your users aren't impacted."

Act 2 — Rapid Diagnosis & Evidence (10–25 minutes)
- Goal: collect 3 signals, test 2 quick mitigations.
- Core checklist (data-first):
  - Confirm request shape: typical tokens in/out, function calls, streaming vs full-response.
  - Check model variant & quantization tier used (hosted/dedicated/private).
  - Observe KV/prefix cache hit rate for that route (last 30m).
  - Check batching behavior: are we hitting batch size limits or long tail queuing?
  - Resource pressure: GPU mem, CPU scheduling, network egress spikes.
- Quick test #1: Pin to a lower-latency model variant for 10 min (explain expected regression in quality).
  - How to: route policy -> model_alias: low-latency-xyz, TTL 10m, monitor p95 and error rate.
- Quick test #2: Turn off streaming in sample requests (if streaming is causing backpressure) or reduce max_tokens for pilot to see throughput improvement.
- Evidence slide: show before/after metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/request, cost delta).
- Speaker notes: emphasize tradeoff: "We’re balancing 10–20% quality regression vs 60–90% reduction in p95 — for user-critical flows we prefer consistent latency."

Act 3 — Commit & Next Steps (5–10 minutes)
- Goal: land on a short-term mitigant + plan to address root cause.
- Options: Temporary fallback -> Expand canary rollout -> Schedule deeper infra move (dedicated capacity)
- Asks to customer:
  - Approve temporary routing change for X hours
  - Share a 24–48h window for a follow-up metric review
  - Agree on acceptance criteria (p95 target, error rate threshold, cost cap)
- Hand-off to Ops: apply routing policy, enable extra logging for the route, start a timeboxed task to investigate hot KV misses.

Slide skeleton (10 slides, quick):
1) Title / 30s summary: "What happened"
2) Signal snapshot (chart + 3 bullet takeaways)
3) Which users/flows impacted (sample request shapes)
4) Quick hypothesis list (prioritized)
5) Quick tests we ran + outcomes (table: test, duration, delta p95, delta cost)
6) Short-term mitigant chosen (config snippet + rollback plan)
7) Ops checklist (who does what, timeline)
8) Acceptance criteria & monitoring (what we watch; alert thresholds)
9) Root-cause next work (owner, ETA)
10) Customer-facing note template + commit

Objection handling cheat snippets (SE-friendly):
- "We can’t accept lower-quality answers" -> "We’ll try a targeted fallback only for this route and monitor a quality sample; if it fails acceptability, we’ll revert automatically. Also, we can A/B with a small percent of traffic to verify."
- "Costs will explode if you change models" -> "We’ll limit the mitigant window and cap burst tokens. We’ll also share an estimated cost delta up front and set an automated rollback if we exceed the cap."
- "We need guaranteed SLAs" -> "For predictable SLOs we recommend Dedicated (reserved pools) or a pinned model variant; this short-term fix is just to stabilize the experience while we scope a commit."

Ops runbook excerpt (for on-call):
- 00:00 — ACK on-call, announce immediate triage channel: #pilot-rescue-<account>
- 00:03 — Run quick metrics script (link below) to capture p95/p99, batch queue length, cache hit rate.
- 00:08 — Implement short-term route (model_alias or fallback_region) with TTL 10–30m; set temporary health check and alert if error rate > 2% in 5m window.
- 00:20 — Re-evaluate; either keep mitigant or roll back.
- 00:30 — Publish internal incident note and schedule root cause analysis with platform eng.
- Quick command snippets (placeholders):
  - redwood route update --route user-facing/qa --model low-latency-1 --ttl 10m --comment "pilot rescue"
  - redwood metrics tail --route user-facing/qa --since 30m --fields p50,p95,p99,cache_hit

Pilot metrics to capture (minimum):
- tokens_per_request (avg + 90th)
- p95 latency for route
- cache_hit_rate (prefix/KV cache)
- batch_queue_time (ms)
- error_rate (4xx/5xx)
- cost_per_1k_tokens (estimated)

Sample customer note (send after Act 1):
"Thanks — we’ve identified a likely cause and will run a short mitigant for up to 30 minutes while we confirm. Expect updates at +10m and +30m. If the temporary change maintains your UX we’ll propose a staged canary with more data."

Slack templates (for SE -> Ops):
"/msg @ops-oncall pilot-rescue <account> p95 spike 1.2s -> running fallback to low-latency-1 for 20m. Initial metrics: p95 1.2s, cache_hit 12%, tokens/request 1.8k. Can you monitor GPU scheduling and network egress?"

Open items / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add concrete runbook commands for Private deployment (customer air-gapped) — currently only hosted examples.
- Bake a small demo (recorded) showing quality tradeoffs: default-model vs low-latency variant for the same prompt set (we need 30 prompts + rubric). Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Confirm exact alert thresholds and automated rollback config with SRE (Leah).
- Small UX ask: add a dashboard tile in Console for quick-hit triage view (tokens/p95/cache) — PM ticket TBD.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is purposely lean; objective is to give SEs a script so they don’t fumble during a live pilot. Looking for: missing quick-tests, any scary rollback scenarios I didn’t consider, better shorthand for the customer-facing language.

References & links:
- Canary checklist (internal): CONFLUENCE-9238
- Pilot metrics dashboard (preprod): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pilot-metrics
- Related playbook: JIRA-GTM-1110 (pilot-ops-cookbook)

Revision history (notes):
- v0.1 created 2026-01-22 (initial script)
- v0.2 2026-02-18: added ops runbook snippet per SRE feedback
- v0.3 2026-03-13: added explicit metric list and Slack templates

End of doc.
